solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Picture he'd held back requires years almost to make sense of

indicators.note: back says the combined piece is read in the opposite direction
held means one piece is gripped inside the other

parts.note: he'd is written out in full letters as HED
PIC is a short form of picture, a photograph

indicators.note: almost says the word for years loses its final letter

parts.note: an era is a span of years

explanation.surface: Someone needs years of study to understand a picture that a man has been keeping back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held back' reads as one phrase meaning 'withheld', but it splits in two: 'held' signals the container and 'back' reverses it. 'requires' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To decode a cipher or puzzling handwriting is to work out its meaning, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Settle in Balmoral area when told to lower stress

indicators.note: when told points to a word spoken, with the stress moved from the first syllable

parts.note: Balmoral Castle stands on Deeside, the valley of the River Dee in Scotland

explanation.surface: Settling in at Balmoral, someone is advised to relax.
explanation.walkthrough: Balmoral is the royal family's Scottish estate on Deeside; said with the stress shifted it gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle a question is to resolve or make a choice about it, a synonym.

clue.text: Ten a penny? He cuts ten times that

indicators.note: cuts means the word breaks into the other piece

parts.note: ten times 'ten a penny' is a hundred a penny: C, A, P
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something sold ten for a penny is undercut by a man charging ten times that.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that' points back to 'Ten a penny', so ten times it is a hundred a penny, with C as the Roman hundred and P for penny.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods so plentiful they sell for a penny per ten are worth very little, so inexpensive.

clue.text: They drop a sport a pro's compromised

indicators.note: compromised means weakened or damaged, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Players who throw a match because a professional has been bribed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drop' suggests losing a game; they drop by parachute. The 's of pro's is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Airborne soldiers descend from aircraft by parachute, so they are troops who drop.

clue.text: King and one born after; alternately K and P

definitions.note: K and P are knit and purl in knitting patterns

parts.note: R, for Rex, is the abbreviation for king
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A royal line of succession, kings and princes taking turns.
explanation.walkthrough: K and P look like king and prince; in a knitting pattern they are knit and purl.
explanation.definitionFit: Ribbing in knitting alternates knit and purl stitches to make a stretchy ridged band.

clue.text: Old English spell cured itch

parts.note: a spell is a turn or go, as in 'have a go'

indicators.note: cured means treated or processed, so the letters of the next word are reworked

explanation.surface: An Anglo-Saxon charm that once cleared up a rash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old English' looks like the language of the spell, but it names a heavy black-letter typeface.
explanation.definitionFit: Old English is the printers' name for a black-letter typeface, otherwise called Gothic script.

clue.text: Medics take this; collapsing they'll get stomach upset — and die

indicators.note: collapsing says the letters of the medics go into the jumble
upset means the combined letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: they'll refers back to the medics, whose letters are part of the pool

explanation.surface: Doctors swear something, then fall ill with stomach trouble and die.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove MEDICS from an anagram of STOMACH DIE and four letters remain: the Hippocratic one doctors swear.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctors traditionally swear the Hippocratic one, a solemn promise of ethical practice.

clue.text: Being unenlightened that chap ruined hen party removing piano

parts.note: he means that chap

indicators.note: ruined means the remaining letters are wrecked into a new order
removing says the letter is taken out

parts.note: taken as written, the letters HENPARTY
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A boorish man wrecks a bachelorette celebration by hauling the piano away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removing' takes P out of HEN PARTY; 'ruined' turns the rest into ATHENRY.
explanation.definitionFit: Paganism, the state of lacking religious enlightenment, is the condition of an unbeliever.

clue.text: Pancake landing in Cambridge cemetery

indicators.note: landing in means coming to rest inside

parts.note: a taco is a Mexican flat pancake folded round a filling

explanation.surface: An aircraft belly-flops onto a Cambridge burial ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pancake landing' suggests a plane's flat crash landing; the pancake is a tortilla.
explanation.definitionFit: An underground gallery with burial recesses, as in Rome, serves as a subterranean cemetery.

clue.text: Root for food

definitions.meaning: to support a team vocally, to shout encouragement

explanation.surface: Reads as a vegetable grown for eating.
explanation.definitionFit: Shouting support for a side is rooting for it; good fare at a festive table is old-fashioned plenty of victuals.

clue.text: Old Homer's heir has black diamonds set in ornament

indicators.note: set in means placed within the other piece

parts.note: Bart is the son of Homer Simpson in the cartoon The Simpsons
jet is a deep glossy black
D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: The heir to an ancient poet inherits jet-black gems mounted in some decoration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Homer' suggests the Greek poet; here it is Homer Simpson, whose son is Bart. 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A small decorative article valued for its artistry is a French-derived term for an ornament or curio.

clue.text: Musical cut short stymies opening box office up. That's awkward

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the whole string is read from the bottom
cut says the final letter is lopped off

parts.note: Evita is the Lloyd Webber and Rice musical
curt means short, brusque

indicators.note: opening means the first letter

explanation.surface: A truncated show blocks the opening of a theatre box office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses EVIT, CURT, S and BO together, reading OB S TRUC TIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone deliberately difficult and unhelpful, putting obstacles in others' way, is being awkward.

clue.text: Supporters of New Year's Day saints and one born on All Fools' Day?

parts.note: January 1st, written Jan I with the Roman numeral

parts.words: one born on All Fools' Day
parts.note: someone born on April 1st falls under the star sign Aries

explanation.surface: A list of red-letter dates: New Year's Day, saints' days and April Fools' birthdays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link. Janissaries were the Ottoman sultan's elite guard; the word extends to loyal followers or henchmen.
explanation.definitionFit: Loyal followers or henchmen of a leader, from the sultan's household troops, are devoted backers.

clue.text: Covering for wings of Dodge stationed in GI's camp

indicators.note: the wings of a word are its two outermost letters

parts.note: to station someone is to put them in place

indicators.note: camp means affected or outrageous, so the letters that follow are rearranged

parts.note: GI's is written as plain letters GIS

explanation.surface: A soldier posted to an American army base stands in for someone at Dodge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'camp' looks like the base; it is the anagram signal shuffling IN and GIS into ISING.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing in for an absent colleague, acting as their substitute, is covering for them.

clue.text: Elegant Windy City long since forgotten

indicators.note: forgotten says that part of the city name is dropped

parts.note: the Windy City is a nickname for Chicago
long since means a long time ago

explanation.surface: A stylish Chicago that has long faded from memory.
explanation.definitionFit: Stylish and fashionable dress or manner is a borrowed French adjective for elegance.

clue.text: Are tarts regularly burnt when baked here?

indicators.note: baked means cooked into a new form, so the letters are rearranged
regularly means every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: Asks whether pastries keep getting scorched in this kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes U and N from 'burnt'; 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The place where tarts are baked and served is an eatery, which 'here' points to.

clue.text: Forcing conformity in vineyards in ever-changing environment

indicators.note: environment means the second piece is surrounded by the first

parts.note: protean, after the shape-shifting sea god Proteus, means constantly changing
crus are French wine-growing estates or vineyards

explanation.surface: Vineyards are being made uniform in a constantly shifting landscape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' joins definition to wordplay, and 'in#2' is a link as well; 'environment' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Procrustes stretched or cut his guests to fit his bed, so his name describes ruthlessly enforced uniformity.

clue.text: Sacrificing one daughter padre made compact with Devil and won

indicators.note: made compact means squeezed into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged
sacrificing means giving up a letter

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter; one of the two Ds goes

explanation.surface: A priest gives up his daughter in a pact with the Devil and wins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link; 'compact' also hints at a pact with the Devil.
explanation.definitionFit: To come out on top or triumph over opposition is to win, so a synonym in the past tense.

clue.text: Soap that's set in a pub?

definitions.text: Soap that's set in a pub?

parts.words: Soap that's set in a pub
parts.note: looks like a TV soap opera set in a pub, but means a solid cake of soap, and also the counter in a pub

explanation.surface: Asks about a television serial whose scenes take place in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: A soap 'set in a pub' recalls Coronation Street's Rovers Return; the answer is a hardened block of soap and the serving counter in a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Soap that has set solid comes as a block, and the pub's serving counter shares that name.

clue.text: Turning out these a girdle's for baking scones with lard

definitions.text: Turning out these a girdle's for baking scones with lard

indicators.note: turning out means remaking, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a girdle's is used as the plain letters AGIRDLES

explanation.surface: A recipe note: a griddle plate is what you use to bake scones made with lard.
explanation.walkthrough: A girdle is the Scots word for a griddle. Shuffle BAKING SCONES LARD and remove the letters of A GIRDLES; what remains spells the Scottish oatcakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat round Scottish scones of oatmeal or barley, baked on a griddle, fit the whole description.

clue.text: Men bent over top of beer mug

indicators.note: bent over says the word is turned back on itself

parts.note: OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers or men

indicators.note: top of means the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: Soldiers hunched over the rim of a beer glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mug' looks like the beer glass; it is the verb to rob someone in the street.
explanation.definitionFit: To mug someone is to attack and steal from them, a synonym for theft.

clue.text: Hoping for change of 10p exactly

indicators.note: change of means the letters are rearranged, while punning on loose change

parts.note: 10p is read as TEN plus P for penny

explanation.surface: Someone hoping to receive precisely ten pence in change.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting while waiting for something one anticipates is to do it in hope, the adverb of anticipation.

clue.text: Commotion or uprising — in Inverness a carfuffle

indicators.note: uprising says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters lie inside the phrase that follows

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An uproar or rising up in the Highland town, a real kerfuffle.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft put 'or' in the definition; it is a link word, so only 'Commotion' defines. 'in' marks the hidden letters, which 'uprising' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: A noisy disturbance or brawl is a commotion, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Retracted, contracted and in order

indicators.note: retracted is read as taken back, so the shortened word is turned around

parts.note: ta'en is the poetic contraction of taken, with the K dropped

explanation.surface: A statement withdrawn, shortened and then put in order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retracted' is re-read as 'taken back': 'contracted' shortens taken to TA'EN, and 'back' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidy and well arranged, everything in its proper place, is a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Subtle Independent got up to interrupt Republican if in turn he stalls

indicators.note: to interrupt means the shuffled letters break into the other pieces
in turn says the little word is reversed

parts.note: taken as written before being turned

indicators.note: got up means dressed or arranged, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A crafty independent senator stands to cut in on a Republican who is stalling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Subtle' looks like a description of the Independent, but it is anagram fodder, and 'got up' is the signal, not 'rose'.
explanation.definitionFit: A politician who talks endlessly to delay a vote in the US Senate is a practitioner of obstruction by speech.

clue.text: Count for instance times I entered the French championship

indicators.note: entered means the letter goes inside

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time, so times gives two Ts
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Count the times I competed in the French championship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Count' looks like a verb; it is the noble rank. 'championship' is a second definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Count is an example of a rank of nobility, a hereditary form of address.

clue.text: Exalted spirits flit about Scottish sky

indicators.note: about means the letters are moved around

explanation.surface: High spirits dart around in the Highland sky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exalted spirits' is a second definition: a boost to morale.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots dialect the heavens or firmament are known by this word.

clue.text: Ring is confining short person in leg-irons

parts.note: to ring someone is to call them on the phone

indicators.note: confining means the two letters wrap around the other piece
short says the word is cut down, leaving only its opening

parts.note: taken as the word person before shortening

explanation.surface: A ring that holds a short man in shackles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short person' suggests a small man, but 'short' means the word person is cut down.
explanation.definitionFit: Metal supports strapped to a weak leg are a kind of brace, nicknamed leg irons.

clue.text: Rus in urbe? Not quite: clearing ugly ruins is the difficulty

indicators.note: clearing means those letters are removed
not quite means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: the letters of ruins in a misshapen order, here S I N U R

explanation.surface: The Latin ideal of country in the city falls short when ugly ruins must be cleared.
explanation.walkthrough: Rus in urbe is Latin for the country in the town. Dropping E leaves RUSINURB; clearing SINUR, the jumbled RUINS, leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: As in Hamlet's 'there's the rub', it means the obstacle or snag.

clue.text: Dido recorded in LA. I can't work that out

indicators.note: work that out means the letters are to be worked into a new arrangement

parts.note: I can't is used as plain letters ICANT

explanation.surface: A record by the singer Dido, made in Los Angeles, baffles the listener.
explanation.walkthrough: Dido looks like the singer; 'dido' is American slang for a prank, hence 'recorded in LA'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dido in American usage is a caper or prank, and a grotesque caper is likewise a playful trick.

clue.text: University governing body, having overlooked name for degree, deliberate

indicators.note: having overlooked one letter for another means swapping it out

parts.note: the senate is the governing body of many universities
D is the abbreviation for degree, as in DD

explanation.surface: A university council, ignoring a nominee for a degree, takes its time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' tells which letter replaces N in SENATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Calm, unhurried and measured in pace is a synonym for deliberate as an adjective.

clue.text: Prop is barring lock

parts.note: but means except or barring, as in 'all but one'
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: A support is preventing a lock from moving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A projecting structure that supports a wall is a prop holding it up.
